Compute SD of length-at-age

get_sd_at_age.Rd

Computes the SD of length at each age from two growth-variability parameters at the reference lengths L1 and L2, under one of two forms selected by sd_model.

Usage

get_sd_at_age(
  mu_a,
  L1,
  L2,
  log_CV1 = NULL,
  log_CV2 = NULL,
  sd_model = "cv",
  log_SD1 = NULL,
  log_SD2 = NULL,
  A1 = NULL,
  A2 = NULL
)

Arguments

mu_a

Numeric vector. Mean length at age (from get_growth). May be AD.

L1

Numeric. Lower reference length, at age A1 (may be AD).

L2

Numeric. Upper reference length, at age A2 (may be AD).

log_CV1

Numeric. Log CV at L1 (may be AD). Used by "cv".

log_CV2

Numeric. Log CV at L2 (may be AD). Used by "cv".

sd_model

Character (data). "cv" (default) or "sd". See Details.

log_SD1

Numeric. Log SD at L1 (may be AD). Used by "sd".

log_SD2

Numeric. Log SD at L2 (may be AD). Used by "sd".

A1, A2

Integer (data). Optional positions in mu_a of the reference ages. When both are supplied, the SD at positions below A1 is held at its value at L1, and the SD at positions A2 and above at its value at L2. When NULL (default), the linear form is extrapolated to all ages.

Value

Numeric vector of SD at each age.

Details

"cv"

CV is linear in mean length, $$CV_a = CV_1 + \frac{\mu_a - L_1}{L_2 - L_1}(CV_2 - CV_1),\quad SD_a = \mu_a CV_a,$$ which is SS3's CV_Growth_Pattern = 0 (CV = f(LAA)). SD is then quadratic in mean length.

"sd"

SD is linear in mean length, $$SD_a = SD_1 + \frac{\mu_a - L_1}{L_2 - L_1}(SD_2 - SD_1),$$ which is SS3's CV_Growth_Pattern = 2 (SD = f(LAA)).

Under both patterns, SS3 holds the CV (or SD) at its young value for ages below A1 and at its old value for ages at or above A2 (SS_ALK.tpl, SS_Label_Info_16.5.3). Supply A1 and A2 to do the same. opal_model supplies them under "sd" only, so "cv" objectives are unchanged.

When SS3's Growth_Age_for_L2 = 999, its upper reference length is Linf, but the SD is still held at the old value from the oldest age. With A2 set to the oldest age, "sd" then matches SS3 at A2 and below A1, and differs slightly in between because the slope uses mu_a[A2] instead of Linf.

References

Stock Synthesis source, SS_ALK.tpl, SS_Label_Info_16.5.2–16.5.4.
